_comment: Asserted byte sizes for istor.fyi's artifact. verify-budget.py fails the build when any of these moves, so a regenerated crop or re-subset font cannot quietly make the site heavier than SITE_DESIGN_PLAN.md §7 says it is. Updating a number here is meant to be a deliberate two-file commit: this file and the design plan's table. Values were measured from disk on 2026-09-18, not transcribed.

totals._note: The payload SITE_DESIGN_PLAN.md §7 prints as 85.4 KB / 113.9 KB. The design plan's phone column is the sum of its own rounded rows; the byte-exact value is 85,345 B. Neither counts the document itself — see document_* below.

document._note: The design plan's payload table omits the document. index.html is real weight and it arrives first, so it is asserted here rather than merely reported. Two numbers, asserted two different ways, and the difference is deliberate. index_html_bytes is a property of the DOCUMENT alone — the artifact is LF-only, so it is identical on every platform — and it is asserted exactly: an edit to the copy deck, or to the stylesheet's CODE rather than its comments, moves it and is meant to. index_html_gzip_ceiling is a property of the document AND of the zlib that compressed it, and Python does not promise byte-stable output across versions, so it is a ceiling with room in it. Measured off the built artifact: 44,812 B raw, 13,772 B gzipped at level 9 with mtime=0 on Python 3.14/Windows; the same bytes compress to 13,722 B on CI's Python 3.12.14/Linux, and that 50 B is what forced the split. On 2026-09-19 the first CI run failed a document it had not touched — the artifact was byte-identical to the reviewed one (120 files, 3,389,782 B, asserted green in the same log) and only the compressed figure differed. A gate that fails on the compressor rather than on the site teaches its reader to ignore it, so the exactness moved to the number that can carry it. The ceiling sits 228 B over the highest figure seen, 1.7%, about five times the spread between the two toolchains: room for a zlib to differ, not for the document to change. It is the compression this check fixes, not the compression a visitor receives — GitHub Pages sets that — so this is a floor on the document's weight and a tripwire on it changing. The tripwire has a history: it read 20,272 B until the stylesheet's comments were stripped on the way in. Comments were 18,949 of styles.css's 34,003 bytes and cost 6,522 B gzipped, 32% of this document, so build-site.py's inline_css() keeps the header comment (1,556 B, the one a reader of view-source needs) and drops the rest; Thoria chose that on 2026-09-18 over shipping all of them or none. It then read 13,750 B until exhibit 09's alt text was repaired, which added 37 B raw and 22 B gzipped for a punctuation fix in one sentence. A comment edit no longer moves it.

library._note: The carried library (SITE_BUILD_PLAN.md §5). Pages are asserted as a count and a total, not file by file — their bytes change the moment anyone edits a summary, and 75 rows of page sizes would assert nothing worth failing over. Shared assets are exact.
